newsitem.title: GERMANY: German confectionery sales may improve in 1997.
newsitem.headline: German confectionery sales may improve in 1997.

text.p: German confectionery sales are expected to be slightly better in 1997 after a disappointingly small rise in 1996 figures, Bernd Monheim, chairman of the confectionery association BDS said.
"The economic environment will only allow for a small rise, prospects aren't rosy," he told a news conference ahead of the annual ISM confectionery trade fair, which runs Jan 26-30.
"We are hoping positive tax signals from the government will fuel consumer spending and the weather in the summer will be good for chocolate sales (which fall in a hot summer)."
The fear of unemployment and wage restraints weighed on consumer spending on food and drinks in 1996 and this was felt very much by confectionery manufacturers, he said.
Planned chocolate price increases might not be accepted by the competitive wholesale and retail sectors.

Projections from market researchers put 1996 joint domestic chocolate and sweets sales up one percent from 2.44 million tonnes in 1995 while sales values should have stagnated at 1995's 18.00 billion marks, BDS said.
This followed two years of losses in both categories.
Chocolate and biscuits sales were higher in 1996 than in 1995 while those of boiled sweets and ice cream declined.
But producers' margins were pressurised as price rises did not fully reflect higher raw materials costs.
Prices of cocoa, raisins and hazelnuts as well as of ingredients derived from grain, vegetable oils and coconut rose because of a weaker mark against the dollar.
Several days of strike action last December over sick pay provisions in the chocolate industry also curtailed revenue in a month usually boosted by seasonal production.

Germany's 120 chocolate firms produced 363,362 tonnes in the first half of 1996, 5.7 percent more than in the same 1995 period while production value, at 3.14 billion marks, was 2.7 percent above the figure a year earlier, BDS said.
But Monheim would not provide production figures for the full year and he could not offer a 1997 forecast.

Gerhard Mollenhauer of the central committee of German retailers (ZAL) said sales of innovative biscuits and chocolate assortments and 200 and 300-gram chocolate tablets were successful, but those of ice cream declined.
